title: Coroner's inquests called into three deaths
article: A coroner's inquest has been called into the death of a Garden Hill teen who hanged himself in a jail cell.
Calvin Waylon McDougall, 19, was found dead May 7 in a cell at the Garden Hill police station. The death was never made public.
Manitoba's chief medical examiner Thambirajah Balachandra called the inquest in accordance with the law that requires an inquest when someone dies in a jail cell.

Inquests have also been called into the deaths of Nathan Michael Boryskavich, 43, of The Pas who died Nov. 29, 2008 after being pepper-sprayed by RCMP, and Maurice Paul Thomas, 45, who died May 7, 2008 at the Health Sciences Centre after he was found lying on the ground near the Disraeli Freeway then taken to Main Street Project where he became unresponsive.
McDougall used a strip of blanket tied to a doorknob in the holding cell to hang himself after he was arrested in Garden Hill for being intoxicated and causing a disturbance.
He was placed in a jail cell by himself at 2:38 a.m., and checked on several times by band police before being found at 6:38 a.m. without a pulse, the coroner's office said.
An autopsy report said the cause of death was hanging and noted McDougall had a blood alcohol level of 262 milligrams. That's more than three times the legal limit for driving.

Thomas, who was found on the ground near the Disraeli Freeway in Winnipeg, had a blood alcohol level of 673 mg and died accidentally of a brain injury caused after he stopped breathing because of acute alcohol intoxication.

Boryskavich died in The Pas after getting into "an altercation" with RCMP responding to a domestic violence complaint. Police pepper-sprayed him and he later died of bleeding on the brain after a traumatic disruption of a right vertebral artery - a sudden twisting of the neck.
The autopsy found he had prescription anti-depressants and sleeping pills in his system with a blood alcohol level of 89 mg.
